brief: TME compiles bank warnings that AI-trade risk has shifted from the narrative itself to its financing and liquidity underpinnings. SocGen's Edwards: excess liquidity has deteriorated sharply, historically a leading indicator for equities, while earnings-upgrade momentum (not earnings itself) has rolled over, a second-derivative risk. Per Bloomberg's White, semis are most yield-curve-sensitive, so curve flattening compounds the liquidity pressure. Jefferies' Wood argues the capex boom ends not from falling demand but if credit markets stop funding it; AI credit spreads have widened sharply, easing only partly. Goldman: AI debt issuance hit $687bn through Nov 3, with hyperscalers alone already past their $250bn full-year forecast at $296bn. BofA: off-balance-sheet AI commitments are up 50%+ quarter-on-quarter, near $3.5tn including Nvidia's newly disclosed obligations. Goldman sizes the revenue hurdle at roughly $350bn a year just to cover 2026-27 depreciation and opex, or over $1tn for the application layer alone. GS's Callahan flags Nvidia-CEO-succession risk to that financing support. Jefferies: AI investment is two-thirds of US GDP growth to Q3. SocGen flags sticky short-term and producer-price inflation. Goldman's counter: hyperscalers remain cash-rich, cloud backlogs are $1.8tn, and the real risk concentrates in leveraged players, not the cash-rich giants.
